.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Small Craft Advisories were extended in time through 2 AM for
the Upper Tidal Potomac and northern portions of Chesapeake Bay.
Frost Advisories and Freeze Warnings remain in effect for the
Alleghenies tonight.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- Below normal temperatures are expected through Sunday night,
  with frost and/or freezing temperatures likely especially 
  west of the Blue Ridge Mountains.

- Showers remain possible at times next week as temperatures 
  rise to near or above normal.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Below normal temperatures are expected through Sunday night, 
with frost and/or freezing temperatures likely especially west 
of the Blue Ridge Mountains.

KEY MESSAGE 1 DESCRIPTION...

Deep closed low north of the Great Lks will maintain a cooler
than normal and unsettled weather pattern through Sunday night.
Several upper air disturbances rotating around this low will
bring the risk of scattered mainly diurnal showers across the
northern half of the fcst area. 

A stronger disturbance will approach the area Saturday leading
to a coastal low pressure development Saturday night and 
Sunday. Recent model trends indicate this low pressure center 
tracking further southeast with all of its associated rainfall 
on the northwest side staying south of our area affecting the
Tidewater region and the southern DelMarVa peninsula. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Showers remain possible at times next week as 
temperatures rise to near or above normal.

KEY MESSAGE 2 DESCRIPTION...

Closed low/longwave troughing will remain centered near/north of the 
Great Lakes early next week. At the surface, a large area of high 
pressure will become positioned in the western Atlantic. Southerly 
winds will become a bit gusty during the daytime, and the ensuing 
warm advection will bring temperatures back closer to or even above 
normal. Some areas could reach 80 on Tuesday. There are some 
uncertainties with how exactly the trough evolves, but a frontal 
zone will be slowly approaching from the northwest Monday and 
Tuesday. Some showers could reach the northwestern half of the 
forecast area as embedded shortwaves pivot through, but overall 
these days should be drier.

At some point during the middle of the week, a digging shortwave 
trough will amplify the pattern and push the cold front across the 
area. This front will bring higher rain chances, and depending on 
timing, potentially thunderstorms. Temperatures will trend back down 
the second half of the week in the wake of the front.

&&

.AVIATION /01Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
NW wind gusts up to 25 kt through 01Z, then winds diminishing
below 10 kt tonight. Scattered showers are expected Fri
afternoon, mainly affecting IAD and MRB. Gusty winds up to 30 kt
are expected Sunday behind a coastal low. 

Southerly winds will gust to 20 kt during the daytime Monday and 
Tuesday. A shower or thunderstorm may reach MRB on Tuesday ahead of 
an approaching frontal zone. Otherwise VFR conditions are
likely.

&&

.MARINE...
Small Craft Advisories have been extended through tonight for
the main Chesapeake Bay channel due to northerly channeling.
Additional SCAs will likely be needed Saturday night into Sunday
as coastal low passes to the southeast.

Small Craft Advisories will be likely Monday and Tuesday in 
southerly flow.
